questions.knowledge_point: Domains of Functions With Trigonometric Components
questions.problem:
The domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=t\,i+\operatorname{csc}⁡(2t)\,j+(1+{t}^{2})\,k$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne .
$$

What is the missing expression? You may assume that $n$ is an integer.
questions.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $t$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $\operatorname{csc}⁡(2t)$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ except for the values of $t$ for which

$$
2t=\pi n\,⟹\,t=\frac{\pi n}{2},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

- The domain of the 3rd component $1+{t}^{2}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is 

$$
t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),\,t\ne \frac{\pi n}{2},
$$

where $n$ is an integer.

- The domain of the 1st component $t+1$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $\operatorname{tan}⁡(3t)$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ except for the values of $t$ for which

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is 

$$

$$

questions.problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(s)=⟨\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-s),\,\sqrt{3}⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\sqrt{s}$ is $s\in [0,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component $\operatorname{ln}⁡(2-s)$ is $s\in (-\infty ,2).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\sqrt{3}$ is $s\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14064302/assets/808abeaa59d7bcea3b24e741fde5296791de32b4170d60f05f2a5af203c20ba2.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(s)$ is $s\in [0,2).$
